outline: 1162 Producing Equivalent Fractions using the Rule

examples.solution_text:
a. Multiples of $8$: $8,16,24,\ldots$
Multiples of $12$: $12,24,\ldots$
The LCD is $24$.
$\frac{5}{8}=\frac{5\times3}{8\times3}=\frac{15}{24}$
$\frac{7}{12}=\frac{7\times2}{12\times2}=\frac{14}{24}$
$\frac{15}{24}>\frac{14}{24}$, so $\frac{5}{8}>\frac{7}{12}$.
b. The only common factor of $9$ and $7$ is $1$, so their LCM is $9\times7=63$.
$\frac{4}{9}=\frac{4\times7}{9\times7}=\frac{28}{63}$
$\frac{3}{7}=\frac{3\times9}{7\times9}=\frac{27}{63}$
$\frac{28}{63}>\frac{27}{63}$, so $\frac{4}{9}>\frac{3}{7}$.

a. The LCD of $6$ and $4$ is $12$.
$\frac{11}{6}=\frac{11\times2}{6\times2}=\frac{22}{12}$
$\frac{7}{4}=\frac{7\times3}{4\times3}=\frac{21}{12}$
$\frac{22}{12}>\frac{21}{12}$, so $\frac{11}{6}>\frac{7}{4}$.
b. Multiples of $15$: $15,30,45,\ldots$
Multiples of $9$: $9,18,27,36,45,\ldots$
The LCD is $45$.
$\frac{10}{15}=\frac{10\times3}{15\times3}=\frac{30}{45}$
$\frac{6}{9}=\frac{6\times5}{9\times5}=\frac{30}{45}$
$\frac{10}{15}=\frac{6}{9}$. Different numerators and denominators can name the same amount.

First write the mixed number as an improper fraction.
$1\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1\times3+2}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$
The LCD of $3$, $8$ and $10$ is $120$.
$\frac{5}{3}=\frac{200}{120}$
$\frac{13}{8}=\frac{195}{120}$
$\frac{17}{10}=\frac{204}{120}$
$\frac{195}{120}<\frac{200}{120}<\frac{204}{120}$
Ascending order: $\frac{13}{8},\ 1\frac{2}{3},\ \frac{17}{10}$.

examples.question_text: Which fraction cannot lie strictly between $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$: $\frac{3}{10}$, $\frac{5}{8}$ or $\frac{4}{6}$?
examples.solution_text:
Write all fractions with denominator $120$.
$\frac{1}{4}=\frac{30}{120}$ and $\frac{2}{3}=\frac{80}{120}$.
$\frac{3}{10}=\frac{36}{120}$, $\frac{5}{8}=\frac{75}{120}$ and $\frac{4}{6}=\frac{80}{120}$.
$30<36<80$ and $30<75<80$, so $\frac{3}{10}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$ lie between the endpoints.
$\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}$ is an endpoint, so it is not strictly between. The answer is $\frac{4}{6}$.
